basics.name: 3D printing service design guides (Hubs / Protolabs Network, Protolabs, Xometry, Formlabs, Prusa)
basics.url: https://www.hubs.com/knowledge-base/design-for-3d-printing/ (Hubs, now 'Protolabs Network', Design for 3D printing index). Key opened articles: https://www.hubs.com/knowledge-base/how-design-snap-fit-joints-3d-printing/ , https://www.hubs.com/knowledge-base/how-design-living-hinges-3d-printing/ , https://www.hubs.com/knowledge-base/how-design-interlocking-joints-fastening-3d-printed-parts/ , https://www.hubs.com/knowledge-base/how-assemble-3d-printed-parts-threaded-fasteners/ ; Protolabs: https://www.protolabs.com/resources/design-tips/how-to-design-3d-printed-hinges/ and https://www.protolabs.com/resources/blog/threading-and-inserts-for-3d-printing/ ; Formlabs: https://formlabs.com/blog/designing-3d-printed-snap-fit-enclosures/ , https://formlabs.com/blog/how-to-3d-print-interlocking-joints/ , https://formlabs.com/blog/adding-screw-threads-3d-printed-parts/ ; Prusa: https://help.prusa3d.com/article/modeling-with-3d-printing-in-mind_164135 , https://blog.prusa3d.com/the-great-guide-to-gluing-and-assembling-3d-prints_44908/ , https://help.prusa3d.com/article/insert-pause-or-custom-g-code-at-layer_120490 . basics.resource_type: PDF design guide (in practice a set of free web design-guide articles and blog posts from 3D printing services and printer makers; a few downloadable white papers)
basics.cost: Free (some Formlabs white papers, e.g. the 'Engineering Fit' tolerance white paper, sit behind a free download form [uncertain])
basics.license: All rights reserved for all of them. Hubs: page footer '(c) 2026 Protolabs Europe B.V. All rights reserved' and its Terms of Use forbid copying, reproducing or republishing any part of the site. Protolabs: '(c) Proto Labs 1999-2026'. Formlabs: '(c) Formlabs'. Prusa blog: no open licence seen on the page [uncertain]. So link to them and cite the numbers, but do not copy text or diagrams
basics.language: English (Hubs also in German, French and Dutch; Prusa Knowledge Base has several translations, e.g. Japanese; Protolabs has regional sites)
basics.year: Mixed: Protolabs 3D-printed hinges tip published 8 Jan 2019, modified 13 Feb 2024; Protolabs threading and inserts blog published 17 May 2022, modified 17 Sep 2026; Prusa gluing guide published 5 Feb 2021, modified 23 Apr 2021; Hubs knowledge base articles are undated on the page but the site was renamed Protolabs Network and the sitemap was updated 21 Sep 2026; Hubs articles probably date from about 2017-2019 when it was '3D Hubs' [uncertain]
basics.access_barrier: none for the articles (Xometry pages returned a bot-check page to scripts; normal browsers pass it [uncertain]); white-paper downloads may need an email form [uncertain]
basics.image_license: Same as text: all rights reserved company photos and diagrams (Hubs uses its own drawings of cantilever and annular snap fits and hinge cross-sections; Protolabs has L = pi R hinge diagrams; Formlabs has photos and CAD screenshots)
basics.authority_level: manufacturer (3D-printing services and printer makers writing design-for-manufacture guidance for their customers; not peer-reviewed, and partly marketing)

coverage.covers: Joining and moving features for 3D-printed parts, spread across roughly 10-15 relevant articles: snap fits (Hubs: cantilever and annular; Formlabs: cantilever, U-shaped, torsion and annular), living hinges (Hubs design rules for FDM, SLS and material jetting; Protolabs MJF/SLS hinge-length formula), interlocking joints (Formlabs: puzzle/jigsaw/tongue, dovetail, key, finger/comb, tenon, scarf joints and print-in-place chain links; Hubs: finger, dovetail and puzzle joints), print-in-place parts (Formlabs chain mail and print-in-place vise), threaded connections (Hubs: heat-set and tap-in inserts, embedded (captive) nuts, self-tapping screws, cut threads, printed threads; Formlabs: screw-to-expand inserts, heat-set inserts, captive nuts, tapping, thread-forming screws, printed threads; Protolabs: heat-stake and press-fit inserts, tapping, chasing), fits and tolerances (clearance, transition, interference), and adhesives (Prusa: cyanoacrylate, solvent cement, two-part epoxy, plus brief notes on PVA, contact cement and methacrylate, with a tensile test). Prusa adds embedding nuts and magnets with a mid-print pause
coverage.organisation: Each company has a blog or knowledge base of standalone articles, grouped loosely by process (FDM, SLA, SLS, MJF) or by topic ('Design for 3D printing', 'Design tips'). Each article is organised as: what it is, types, which process and material, tolerances, best practices, FAQ. This works well for a beginner who already knows the name ('snap fit', 'living hinge'), but there is no cross-company index and no way to start from a need such as 'I want a lid that clicks shut'
coverage.scope_match: high for the 3D-printing priority: they are the main practical source for snap fits, living hinges, print-in-place and interlocking joints, heat-set inserts and captive nuts, with real clearance numbers. Low for everything else (no gear trains, no powered connectors, few clever mechanisms)
coverage.taxonomy_used: No formal taxonomy. Snap fits are split by shape of the flexing part (cantilever, U-shaped, torsion, annular) and by permanent vs releasable; threaded joining is split by method (insert, embedded nut, self-tapping screw, tapped thread, printed thread); interlocking joints by shape (puzzle, dovetail, key, finger, tenon, scarf, chain link); adhesives by chemistry (cyanoacrylate, solvent, two-part epoxy, other). About 4-6 families of joining method in total
coverage.example_types: cantilever snap fit; U-shaped snap fit; torsion snap fit; annular snap fit (bottle-cap / pen-cap style); living hinge (FDM single-strand, SLS/MJF nylon, multi-material TPU hinge); print-in-place chain links (chain mail); print-in-place vise; puzzle / jigsaw joint; dovetail joint; key joint; finger (comb) joint; tenon joint; scarf joint; locating lugs; heat-set threaded insert; tap-in (press-fit) insert; screw-to-expand insert; captive (embedded) hex nut in a nut pocket; thread-forming (self-tapping) screw for plastics; printed semicircular-profile thread; magnets embedded with a mid-print pause; cyanoacrylate (superglue), solvent cement (acetone for ABS/ASA), two-part epoxy
coverage.making_methods: 3D printing: FDM/FFF (Prusa, Hubs), SLA resin (Formlabs), SLS, MJF and material jetting (Hubs, Protolabs, Formlabs); some links to injection-moulding practice
coverage.item_count: About 10-15 relevant articles across the five companies (Hubs design-for-3D-printing index lists 49 knowledge-base links, of which about 5 are about joining; Formlabs about 3-4 relevant posts; Protolabs about 3-4; Prusa 2-3). Roughly 20-25 distinct joint or fastening types in total
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: Compliant: yes (snap fits and living hinges, with strain and thickness guidance). Print-in-place: partly (Formlabs chain links and print-in-place vise; Prusa suggests at least 0.3 mm gap for moving parts). Hand-release only: partly (releasable vs permanent snap fits set by undercut shape). Adhesive types: yes in the Prusa guide (cyanoacrylate incl. gel, rubber-filled, odourless and thin grades; solvent cements matched to plastics: acetone for ABS/ASA, limonene for HIPS, isopropyl alcohol for PVB, PETG inert; two-part epoxy; PVA and contact cement mentioned). Torque-limiting, self-locking, one-way/ratchet, indexing/detent, over-centre, gear trains, powered connectors: not covered in the articles opened
coverage.entry_structure: Article with a definition, photos and simple diagrams, a table of process suitability, numeric design rules (thickness, clearance, fillet ratio), best-practice bullets, FAQ, and a call to get a quote; Formlabs adds step-by-step CAD tutorials and a video; Hubs embeds a YouTube tutorial
coverage.audience_level: hobbyist to professional (written for engineers ordering parts, but plain enough for hobbyists; Prusa is aimed at home FDM users)

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: high: short plain-language explanations, photos of real printed parts, clear rules of thumb (for example 0.5 mm clearance for FDM), little maths except the Protolabs hinge formula and the Formlabs strain discussion
usefulness.has_images: yes: good-quality photos of printed parts and clean diagrams (snap-fit types, hinge cross-sections with dimensions, interlocking joint shapes, insert installation), all company-owned
usefulness.has_animations: some video: Hubs embeds a YouTube snap-fit tutorial and has a 'Watch and learn' video section; Formlabs threads article includes an application video; no interactive models
usefulness.gaps: Scattered across five sites with no shared index or selector; no single page compares snap fit vs hinge vs insert vs glue for a given job; numbers disagree slightly between companies (FDM clearance 0.5 mm at Hubs vs 0.3 mm for moving parts at Prusa); little on clever mechanisms (ratchets, detents, bayonets, cam locks, torque limiters), nothing on gears or powered latches; much is written for SLS/MJF service parts rather than home FDM; Xometry content could not be checked [uncertain]; marketing calls to action interrupt the text
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: yes: stable, descriptive per-topic URLs, e.g. https://www.hubs.com/knowledge-base/how-design-snap-fit-joints-3d-printing/ for snap fits, https://www.hubs.com/knowledge-base/how-design-living-hinges-3d-printing/ for living hinges, https://formlabs.com/blog/how-to-3d-print-interlocking-joints/ for dovetail and puzzle joints, https://www.hubs.com/knowledge-base/how-assemble-3d-printed-parts-threaded-fasteners/ for heat-set inserts and captive nuts, https://blog.prusa3d.com/the-great-guide-to-gluing-and-assembling-3d-prints_44908/ for glue types. Hubs changed brand to Protolabs Network but kept hubs.com URLs
usefulness.reusable_data: not reusable beyond linking and citing facts: all rights reserved, and the Hubs Terms of Use forbid copying or building a competing site from its content. Scrape-only HTML (Hubs has an XML sitemap at https://www.hubs.com/sitemap.xml)
usefulness.maintained: yes: all sites are live and commercial; Protolabs threading article modified Sep 2026; Hubs sitemap updated Sep 2026; Prusa gluing guide last modified 2021 but still online; Hubs pages carry the 2026 copyright
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) One clear number per process (clearance 0.5 mm FDM, 0.3 mm SLS/SLA/MJF) shown as a small table on each entry. (2) Hubs' 'best practices' mini-illustrations: taper the beam, fillet the root, widen the clip, only deflect during assembly, avoid Z-direction flexing, add lugs. (3) Protolabs' hinge-length rule L = (bend angle / 180) x pi x R, with a picture of too-short vs too-long hinges. (4) Formlabs' 'which joint type' gallery with a one-line verdict per type ('good for 3D printing' / 'not ideal'). (5) Prusa's glue guide structure: rule of thumb, which glue for which plastic, warnings, then a simple strength test table; also the 'reversible?' question (debonder for CA). (6) Comparing threaded options in one table (insert vs captive nut vs self-tapping vs printed thread) by strength and reusability
usefulness.design_rules_given: Yes, many numbers: Hubs snap fits: clearance 0.5 mm FDM, 0.3 mm SLS/SLA/MJF/material jetting; cantilever base at least 1 mm thick with at least 1 mm overhang (MJF); root fillet at least 0.5 x base thickness; width at least 5 mm. Hubs living hinges: FDM 0.4-0.6 mm thick (at least two layers), SLS 0.3-0.8 mm thick and at least 5 mm long (30-50 cycles), material jetting 0.4-0.8 mm; anneal in boiling water. Protolabs hinges: thickness equal to minimum feature size (0.02 in MJF, 0.03 in SLS), L = pi R; split one wide hinge into several narrow ones. Hubs interlocking joints: 0.5 mm FDM, 0.2 mm SLA/SLS, 0.1 mm material jetting. Formlabs: 0.2 mm gap for small parts, 0.4 mm for chunky ones; printed threads M6 or 1/4-20 and larger, semicircular thread profile with 0.1 mm offset for small threads. Hubs threads: wall around a thread at least the screw diameter (M5 needs 5 mm); avoid FDM printed threads below M5; captive nut offset 0.2 mm total; pilot hole for 75-80% thread engagement. Protolabs: 0.25 in (6.35 mm) clearance around heat-stake inserts; screw-to-expand inserts with epoxy for SLA. Prusa: printer accurate to 0.2 mm; at least 0.3 mm for moving parts; CA keeps about 50% strength at 80 C
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: No generators; Formlabs links a downloadable STL enclosure on Pinshape and CAD step-by-steps, nothing parametric
usefulness.file_formats: HTML articles with images, embedded YouTube video; downloadable PDF white papers (Formlabs, Hubs reports) and occasional STL example files
usefulness.terminology_value: medium: good for maker-level names and aliases (snap fit = connector = clip; hook = bead = head; undercut; lugs; heat-set vs tap-in vs screw-to-expand inserts; thread-forming = self-tapping; captive nut = nut boss; capillary gluing; CA frosting (blooming), debonder), but not a formal standard vocabulary and no translations beyond Hubs' four languages
usefulness.decision_support: Process-suitability tables (FDM vs SLA vs SLS vs material jetting for snap fits and interlocking joints, star ratings in Formlabs), the Hubs threaded-fastener method table with one-line pros and cons, the Prusa glue-to-plastic compatibility notes and tensile test table. No flow chart or interactive selector
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Snap-fit theory comes from plastics makers' injection-moulding manuals (Bayer/Covestro, BASF) and Formlabs explicitly points readers to an MIT snap-fit design guide; living-hinge geometry is adapted from injection-moulding practice. Hubs and Protolabs are now the same group (Protolabs Network), so count them as related sources. Hubs content overlaps with its own 'The 3D Printing Handbook' book [uncertain]. Heavy overlap with CNC Kitchen insert tests, Makelab and other service bureau guides found in search
